plain_description.what: Leaves one corpus out and feeds it into the trees of the other five corpora one question at a time (filing, out-of-scope buffering, refitting the cell means). It compares this with a batch rebuild, and checks how many existing cell addresses move. No judge calls.
plain_description.why: It asks whether the tree can absorb a new domain online without moving existing addresses, and how close it gets to a full rebuild.
plain_description.information: Small loss and stable addresses would support online updating in deployment. Result: done. Online replay files 3.9pp worse than a batch rebuild (interval -5.1 to -2.6pp; one draw). Refitting the means moved 9.25% of existing addresses when BBH was added (3% for MMLU-Pro), so addresses stay stable only if the means are frozen. The claim that 'ids are immutable' online narrows accordingly. The tree vs k-means comparison is descriptive only.
